docs.title: Polars Genson
docs.text: Fast JSON schema inference with support for Polars DataFrames.

docs.title: Project Structure

docs.title: Python Package
docs.text: • polars-genson-py/ - Python bindings and Polars plugin

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
pip install polars-genson[polars]

import polars as pl
import polars_genson

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "json_data": [
        '{"name": "Alice", "age": 30, "scores": [95, 87]}',
        '{"name": "Bob", "age": 25, "city": "NYC", "active": true}'
    ]
})

json_schema = df.genson.infer_json_schema("json_data")
polars_schema = df.genson.infer_polars_schema("json_data")

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fast schema inference from JSON strings in Polars columns
  • Dual output formats: JSON Schema and native Polars schemas
  • Complex type support: nested objects, arrays, mixed types
  • Multiple JSON formats: single objects, arrays, NDJSON
  • Rust performance with Python convenience

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text:
• write_parquet writes Arrow data with genson's Parquet writer. Any object with __arrow_c_stream__ (a pyarrow table or record batch reader, a Polars frame, genson's Arrow stream) is written as genson writes its own output, each row group's leaf columns encoded in parallel with the GIL released, its buffers not copied. Wikidata's claims statements (1.56 million deeply nested rows) write in 2.3 s on 4 threads against pyarrow's 8.5 s, 5% smaller, with the same schema and data as pyarrow writes. In Rust, genson_core::parquet::write_arrow_batches.
  • Tall flat Parquet output is smaller. Data pages end at 1 MiB, as Polars' do, rather than every 20,000 rows (arrow-rs's default). zstd compresses each page on its own, so larger pages compress better: a 12.5-million-row table of a string and an Int64 column is 7.7% smaller (67.6 MB to 62.4 MB, under Polars' 62.6 MB), and a 94-column table 3.0% smaller. Tables of fewer than 20,000 rows, and nested columns whose pages already reached 1 MiB first, are written byte for byte as before.
  • Parquet output dictionary-encodes only columns whose values repeat. A leaf column whose first values are mostly distinct (more than three quarters, as Polars decides) is written without a dictionary, which cost a hash per value and grew the file until arrow-rs gave the dictionary up: a table of 94 near-unique columns writes 2.5 times faster and 25% smaller. No file is larger; Wikidata claims are 0.5% smaller.
  • Narrow tables write faster. genson's Parquet writer encodes several row groups at once, each leaf column of each a task of its own, where it encoded one row group at a time: a table of a few columns and many rows uses every thread rather than one (a 25-million-row string column: 2.4 s to 0.8 s on 4 threads). The file is unchanged, byte for byte.
  • Typed Parquet output can be written in a stored schema. normalise_from_parquet takes schema (a pl.Schema or pl.Struct), checked against the inferred schema before anything is written (schema_check="compatible", "strict" or "none"), and unnest=True to write the struct's fields as top-level columns. Fields the file lacks are written as nulls and the file is laid out as Polars writes the same frame, so chunks inferred separately share one schema without reading the output back to conform it. check_schema_compatibility gives the same verdict for two schemas. On a 10,000-entity chunk of the Wikidata dump, writing the claims this way took 3.0 s where genson's output read back, conformed and written again by Polars took 30 s.
  • normalise_json(decode=False) is faster. It parsed every row into a Value, normalised it and serialised it; rows now go through the typed decoder into Arrow and are written back as JSON, with the same text. Rows the typed decoder declines, and inputs too few rows for the schema's width to pay for its columns, take the old path.
  • no_unify works through the DataFrame.genson methods. infer_json_schema, infer_polars_schema and normalise_json on df.genson accepted no_unify but never passed it on, so a map candidate holding a key it names was still unified into a map. The expression functions (polars_genson.infer_json_schema and the rest) were not affected.
  • DataFrame.genson.normalise_json decodes rows straight into Polars dtypes. With decode=True (the default) it inferred the schema twice, once to normalise and once for the dtypes, then wrote every row out as JSON text for str.json_decode to parse again. It now infers once and normalises the rows straight into Arrow, as typed normalise_from_parquet output does: 2.3–8.8× faster on 1,000 label maps, 20,000 event logs, 200,000 small records and a chunk of Wikidata claims, with less than half the peak memory on most, and the same frames. Rows the direct decoder cannot take, and decode=<schema>, still go by way of JSON text.
  • A key that is a list in some places and a record or scalar in others keeps its values. Such a field inferred as a union of the list and the other types, and both avro_to_polars_schema and normalisation take a union's first branch: normalisation wraps a record or scalar into the list, but the list's items did not hold its fields or type, so its values were dropped ({"d": 9} beside [{"d": null}] gave d: null, as in #238), or, with the record first, every list was. The union is now one list whose items unify the list's items with the other branches (records fieldwise, scalars promoted to __integer-style fields as among a list's records), so every value is kept, whichever comes first, beside null or not. Branches the items cannot unify with (different scalars, a branch of several types), and every union with wrap_scalars=False, stay as they were.
  • A field that is a scalar in some rows and an empty list in the rest decodes. Its Avro schema typed the list's items null (the list was empty in every row), but normalisation wraps the scalar into the list, so normalise_json's output (["x"] under List(Null)) failed to decode, whatever empty_as_null. Such a list's items now take the scalars' types (List(String), holding ["x"]). Schemas change only there: a list that is ever non-empty is as before.
  • A value where the schema types null normalises to null, so the rows decode. A record field or a list's items typed null (as the Avro conversion types those only ever null or empty) kept any value given there as it was, though the column is Null and cannot hold it: normalise_json's output failed to decode. Such a value reaches there when a union's other branch is wrapped into its first. It is now null, as a value a field's type cannot hold is anywhere else, and the typed decoder takes these rows rather than leaving them to the slower path. Output changes only there: with decode=False, the JSON held the value; decoded, it failed.
  • A field forced to a map keeps its values' type when it is a scalar in some rows. force_field_types={"labels": "map"} on a field that held {"en": "x"} in some rows and "s" in others (or only ever "s") gave a map of null values, as the union, the type list (["object", "string"]) or the scalar type left it no properties to read its values from; normalisation kept the strings regardless only because a null-typed value passed through. Such a map now takes its records' values with the scalar, which normalisation wraps into the map as a value (labels__string): map<string> here, map<int> for integers, strings where they differ. On Wikidata claims fixtures, the forced labels maps hold strings where they held null.
  • A map only ever empty, or holding nulls alone, unifies with one holding values. Its values are typed null, and unifying it with a map of typed values failed: the records holding them were not unified, so a field of such records was not inferred as a map (a map with {} in one row beside {"en": "x"} in another). Values typed null now join typed ones as null does: the map holds the type, nullable (null and string), so the nulls a map may hold stay possible; two maps of null values stay null. In a record's field, two maps whose values differ only in being nullable now unify too. Schemas change only where such maps failed to unify.
  • Normalisation no longer panics on a field whose type is null alone. The Avro conversion can give a record the fields of a differently shaped one that shares its name (#238, avrotize-rs#28), leaving a field typed ["null"] where the data holds values. Normalising such a value panicked; it is now null, as a value a field's type cannot hold is anywhere else. The record's lost fields are a separate bug, in the conversion.

• A field some map values lack is no longer required. Map unification made a record field required (and its Avro field non-nullable) whenever every record it unified listed the field, though a record that was itself unified lists every field seen so far, required or not. A record field missing from some values could then be required, depending on the order of the values, and normalised output held a record of nulls where the field was missing; it now holds null. Schemas change only by fields dropped from required and made nullable.

  • Inference, normalisation and Parquet I/O do far less work (#256). Inference reads each row once as interned states and rewrites the merged schema as a hash-consed DAG, never writing it out. Normalisation compiles the schema into a plan once (NormalisePlan in genson-core) and writes rows straight into Arrow, and the normalise_json expression normalises its rows in parallel. Values are moved rather than copied. Inferred schemas and normalised output are unchanged, except by the two fixes in this release. On genson-core's scorecard corpora (scripts/scorecard.py: instructions on one thread, wall time on 4 threads), from 1.0.2 with the row-hashing change below to 1.0.3:

    corpus instructions wall time claims (2,000 Wikidata-like rows, wikidata-pq's options) −91% 1,762 → 233 ms events (20,000 event logs) −77% 90 → 17 ms narrow (100,000 small records) −81% 186 → 23 ms labels (1,000 label maps) −54% 171 → 83 ms entities (150 wide entities) −59% 201 → 81 ms the claims, normalised −78% 1,109 → 423 ms

    A field forced to "map" takes the slower per-row path: 20% fewer instructions there, with no measurable change in time. These are genson-core's workloads; the Python package runs the same code. - Parquet output is zstd-compressed. genson wrote every Parquet file uncompressed; typed output, string output, lookup tables and pruned values are now written with zstd (level 1). On 200 rows of Wikidata claims the typed output is 5 MB where it was 16 MB, in the same time, and the normalised JSON 27 MB where it was 212 MB. - normalise_from_parquet and infer_from_parquet decode only their column. Reading one column decoded every column of the file, and each row was then copied into a String; the column is now decoded alone and its rows borrowed from the Arrow arrays. On a chunk of wikidata-pq's shape (3,000 rows, 332 MB of claims beside the labels, descriptions, aliases and sitelinks), its three map steps take 0.7–0.8 s where they took 3.5–4.6 s. - extract_invariants reads each row's text once. Each row was parsed into a tree, the fields removed and the row written out again; rows are now scanned as text, with the removed fields cut out, and only rows the scan cannot read exactly as before (invalid JSON, a line break, a repeated or escaped key in an object with fields removed) take the old path. The lookup table, the inferred schema and the normalised output are unchanged. On 3,000 rows of wikidata-pq's claims (332 MB, 98% of it the label maps removed), extraction takes 0.2–0.3 s where it took 0.7–0.8 s. With two values for one key, the error now names the first in row order. In genson-core's extract_invariants, the slim rows keep their own spacing and escapes instead of serde_json's compact form. - Parquet string columns are decoded in parallel. Where the file has an offset index (Polars and arrow-rs write one) or several row groups, the column is split into row ranges of about equal size, each decoded by its own reader. Decoding the claims of a chunk written as wikidata-pq writes them (Polars, zstd level 9) takes 0.05–0.06 s on 4 cores where it took 0.3–0.4 s. - An integer beyond the 64-bit range no longer panics. Inference read it with simd-json, which failed on it after serde_json had accepted the input; it is now a number, as serde_json reads it when normalising. - Less time spent deduplicating rows. Given 10 or more strings, inference hashes each string's schema to skip duplicates; a scalar field is now hashed without building its schema, for 6–17% less CPU time on Wikidata claims and on narrow rows. SchemaBuilder::schema_hash gives the same values as before.

• SchemaBuilder::add_schemas keeps what the builder already held (genson-core Rust API). Given schemas with more than 3 properties between them, it replaced the builder's schema for each of those properties instead of merging into it. Inference, genson-cli and the Python package do not call it.

• A key missing from some objects is no longer required. When a field's objects were merged, those holding no key in common were not counted, so a key could be marked required (and its Avro field non-nullable) although some rows lack it, and which keys were required could depend on the order of the rows or vary from run to run. Schemas change only by keys dropped from required.
  • wrap_root wraps each document as written. Duplicate keys and number formatting now reach inference unchanged, as without wrap_root.
  • Faster inference. About twice as fast on Wikidata claims with unify_maps, and on large rows with default options. See How inference works.

A JSON object genson infers as a map is now a Polars map, pl.Map, wherever genson gives Polars data or dtypes, and a Parquet MAP in typed output. See Map types.

  • Polars ≥ 2 is required. import polars_genson raises ImportError on Polars 1.x.
  • Maps are pl.Map by default. map_encoding defaults to "mapping" throughout the Python package, as in genson-core and genson-cli: infer_polars_schema, avro_to_polars_schema and normalise_json(decode=True) give pl.Map(pl.String, V), JSON string output writes each map as an object ({"en": "Hello"}), and normalise_from_parquet(typed=True) writes Parquet maps. Pass map_encoding="kv" for lists of {key, value} structs, as before.
  • normalise_json(decode=schema) decodes maps in the schema's shape: a pl.Map from objects, a list of {key, value} structs from key/value lists, unless map_encoding is given.
  • schema_to_dict renders a pl.Map as {"map": {"key": ..., "value": ...}}.
  • genson-core's avro_to_arrow_type and avro_record_fields take native_map, which writes an Avro map as an Arrow Map in place of a list of {key, value} structs.

• infer_polars_schema and avro_to_polars_schema take map_encoding. Each map gets the dtype its encoding decodes to, so a schema can be asked for in the shape the data was normalised in. "kv", the default, gives the list of {key, value} structs as before. polars-jsonschema-bridge now names a map Map[String,V] in place of List[Struct[key:String,value:V]], which the infer_polars_schema expression shows.

• normalise_from_parquet(prune=...) removes malformed records. Every record holding one of the named fields is removed during normalisation and written to prune_output_path, and the fields are left out of the output schema. See Remove malformed records. genson-cli has --prune and --prune-output.

• normalise_json(decode=schema) accepts a pl.Schema, such as one from infer_polars_schema, as its docstring says. It previously raised TypeError.
  • Fields forced to "map" keep their values' type. force_field_types={"x": "map"} used to make every value a string; now a map of integers stays a map of integers, and values fall back to strings only when they have no common type. See Maps and records.
This release fixes several ways genson silently lost or mistyped data, makes inferred field order deterministic, and adds extract_invariants for JSON that embeds repeated data.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
• Polars ≥ 1.43.2 is required. genson writes Parquet with parquet 60, which marks float columns with the IEEE 754 total column order, and Polars before 1.43.2 can't read typed output that has a float column.
  • Python ≥ 3.10 is required, because Polars 1.43.2 requires it.
  • The polars-lts-cpu extra is replaced by rtcompat, following Polars: pip install polars-genson[rtcompat].
  • infer_polars_schema defaults to avro=True, so it reports the dtypes that normalise_json and typed Parquet output produce. Pass avro=False for the old route.

docs.title: Output changes
docs.text:
• A field that is sometimes a scalar and sometimes an object keeps its scalars under a promoted field__string-style key by default. See Mixed types.
  • Integers in a float field become floats (1 → 1.0) instead of null.
  • Arrays that are empty in every row get the dtype List(Null) instead of List(Boolean).
  • Field order follows the order keys appear in the JSON, for objects of any size. Objects of more than 32 keys previously gave a different order on each run. See Field order.
  • JSON Schema to Polars conversion maps objects with additionalProperties to List(Struct{key, value}), and nullable types to their non-null type.

docs.title: New
docs.text: • extract_invariants on normalise_from_parquet: moves fields that are invariant per key into a lookup table before inference. See Factor out repeated embedded data.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: polars-genson turns a column of JSON strings into typed Polars columns. It infers a schema from the JSON, then rewrites every row to fit that schema, so rows that differ (missing keys, extra keys, empty arrays, varying object keys) all end up in one consistent set of columns.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install polars-genson[polars]

On older CPUs, use Polars' compatibility runtime instead:

pip install polars-genson[rtcompat]

polars-genson needs Python 3.10 or later and Polars 1.43.2 or later.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Here are three rows of JSON that don't agree on their shape: city is sometimes missing, tags is sometimes empty, and scores has different keys in each row.

import polars as pl
import polars_genson  # registers the .genson namespace on DataFrames

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "json": [
        '{"id": 1, "name": "Ada", "city": "London", "tags": ["x", "y"], "scores": {"maths": 90}}',
        '{"id": 2, "name": "Bob", "tags": [], "scores": {"art": 75, "history": 60}}',
        '{"id": 3, "name": "Cy", "city": "Oslo", "tags": ["z"], "scores": {"maths": 80, "art": 70}}',
    ]
})
print(df.genson.infer_polars_schema("json", map_threshold=1))

Schema({'id': Int64, 'name': String, 'city': String, 'tags': List(String), 'scores': Map(String, Int64)})

infer_polars_schema reads every row and reports one Polars schema that fits them all. scores becomes a pl.Map, because its keys vary from row to row and map_threshold=1 lets genson treat it as a map rather than a record with fixed fields.

To get the data itself in that shape, use normalise_json:

print(df.genson.normalise_json("json", map_threshold=1))

shape: (3, 5)
┌─────┬──────┬────────┬────────────┬────────────────────────────┐
│ id  ┆ name ┆ city   ┆ tags       ┆ scores                     │
│ --- ┆ ---  ┆ ---    ┆ ---        ┆ ---                        │
│ i64 ┆ str  ┆ str    ┆ list[str]  ┆ map[str, i64]              │
╞═════╪══════╪════════╪════════════╪════════════════════════════╡
│ 1   ┆ Ada  ┆ London ┆ ["x", "y"] ┆ {"maths": 90}              │
│ 2   ┆ Bob  ┆ null   ┆ null       ┆ {"art": 75, "history": 60} │
│ 3   ┆ Cy   ┆ Oslo   ┆ ["z"]      ┆ {"maths": 80, "art": 70}   │
└─────┴──────┴────────┴────────────┴────────────────────────────┘

Every row now has every column. The missing city is null, and the empty tags list is null too (pass empty_as_null=False to keep it as []).

20 map_max_required_keys int

Maximum number of required keys allowed for Map inference. Objects with more required keys will be forced to Record type. If None, no gating based on required key count.

None unify_maps bool

Enable unification of compatible but non-homogeneous record schemas into maps. When True, record schemas with compatible field types can be merged into a single map schema with selective nullable fields.

False no_unify set[str] | None

Prevent unification of keys under these field names with their sibling record fields.

None force_field_types dict[str, str]

Explicit overrides for specific fields. Values must be "map" or "record". Example: {"labels": "map", "claims": "record"}.

None force_parent_field_types dict[str, str]

Explicit overrides for fields based on their parent field name. Values must be "map" or "record". Example: {"labels": "map", "claims": "record"}.

None force_scalar_promotion set[str]

Set of field names that should always be promoted to wrapped scalars, even when they appear as simple scalars. Ensures schema stability for fields known to have heterogeneous types across chunks. Example: {"precision", "datavalue"}.

None wrap_scalars bool

Whether to promote scalar values into singleton objects when they appear in contexts where other rows provide objects, or scalars of another kind (an integer and a string, not an integer and a number). This keeps every value with its type, where the union would keep one kind. The promoted field name defaults to the parent key with a __{type} suffix, e.g. a string under "value" becomes {"value__string": "..."}.

True coerce_strings bool

Infer the dtypes for rows that normalise_json(coerce_strings=True) normalises: strings beside numbers or booleans are to be coerced to them, so they are not given fields of their own.

False avro bool

Whether to infer and convert through an Avro schema (the default) or through JSON Schema. The Avro route reports the dtypes that normalise_json produces (maps as map_encoding decodes them, one branch of a union). The JSON Schema route falls back to String for unions and nullable fields.

True map_encoding ('mapping', 'entries', 'kv')

The map_encoding the JSON is normalised with: each map gets the dtype that encoding decodes to, a pl.Map for "mapping" and a list of {key, value} structs for "kv". "entries" has none, and raises ValueError if the schema holds a map.

"mapping" wrap_root str | bool | None

If a string, wrap each JSON row under that key before inference. If True, wrap under the column name. If None, leave rows unchanged.

None no_root_map bool

Prevent document root from becoming a map type, even if it meets map inference criteria

True max_builders int

Maximum number of schema builders to create in parallel at once. Lower values reduce peak memory usage during schema inference. If None, processes all strings at once. Default is None.

        even when they appear as simple scalars. Ensures schema stability for
        fields known to have heterogeneous types across chunks.
        Example: ``{"precision", "datavalue"}``.
    wrap_scalars : bool, default True

        in contexts where other rows provide objects, or scalars of another kind

    -------

    """
    if not merge_schemas:
        raise NotImplementedError("Only merge schemas is implemented")
    fft = (
        {}
        if force_field_types is None
        else {"force_field_types": force_field_types}
    )
    fpft = (
        {}
        if force_parent_field_types is None
        else {"force_parent_field_types": force_parent_field_types}
    )
    wrap_root_field = column if wrap_root is True else wrap_root
    result = self._df.select(
        infer_polars_schema(
            pl.col(column),
            ignore_outer_array=ignore_outer_array,
            ndjson=ndjson,
            merge_schemas=merge_schemas,
            debug=debug,
            profile=profile,
            verbosity=verbosity,
            map_threshold=map_threshold,
            map_max_required_keys=map_max_required_keys,
            unify_maps=unify_maps,
            no_unify=no_unify,
            **fft,
            **fpft,
            force_scalar_promotion=(
                list(force_scalar_promotion) if force_scalar_promotion else []
            ),
            wrap_scalars=wrap_scalars,
            coerce_strings=coerce_strings,
            avro=avro,
            wrap_root=wrap_root_field,
            no_root_map=no_root_map,
            max_builders=max_builders,
        ).first()
    )

    # Extract the schema from the first column, which is the struct
    schema_fields = result.to_series().item()
    return pl.Schema(
        {
            field["name"]: _parse_polars_dtype(field["dtype"], map_encoding)
            for field in schema_fields
        }
    )

        # onto it where that is exactly what json_decode makes of the JSON text. A
        # dtype holding one the typed route never makes goes to the text route
        typed = None
        if decode is True or typed_route_makes(dtype):
            typed = _rust_normalise_json_typed(
                self._df.get_column(column),
                orjson.dumps(
                    _normalise_kwargs(
                        ignore_outer_array=ignore_outer_array,
                        ndjson=ndjson,
                        empty_as_null=empty_as_null,
                        coerce_strings=coerce_strings,
                        map_encoding=map_encoding,
                        profile=profile,
                        map_threshold=map_threshold,
                        map_max_required_keys=map_max_required_keys,
                        unify_maps=unify_maps,
                        no_unify=no_unify,
                        force_field_types=force_field_types,
                        force_parent_field_types=force_parent_field_types,
                        force_scalar_promotion=force_scalar_promotion,
                        wrap_scalars=wrap_scalars,
                        wrap_root=wrap_root_field,
                        no_root_map=no_root_map,
                        max_builders=max_builders,
                        avro_schema=avro_schema,
                    )
                ).decode(),
            )
        if typed is not None:
            series, normalised_schema = typed
            inferred = pl.Struct(
                avro_to_polars_schema(normalised_schema, map_encoding=map_encoding)
            )
            result = series.cast(inferred).to_frame()
            if decode is True:
                return result.unnest(column) if unnest else result
            projected = project_dtype(pl.col(column), inferred, dtype)
            if projected is not None:
                result = result.select(projected.alias(column))
                if result.schema[column] == dtype:
                    return result.unnest(column) if unnest else result
            # Otherwise the JSON text route, decoded by json_decode itself
        if decode is True and avro_schema is not None:
            dtype = pl.Struct(
                avro_to_polars_schema(
                    avro_schema
                    if isinstance(avro_schema, str)
                    else orjson.dumps(avro_schema).decode(),
                    map_encoding=map_encoding,
                )
            )
        elif decode is True:
            # Infer Avro schema and convert it to Polars Schema
            schema = self.infer_polars_schema(
                column,
                ignore_outer_array=ignore_outer_array,
                ndjson=ndjson,
                merge_schemas=True,
                profile=profile,
                map_threshold=map_threshold,
                map_max_required_keys=map_max_required_keys,
                unify_maps=unify_maps,
                no_unify=no_unify,
                force_field_types=force_field_types,
                force_parent_field_types=force_parent_field_types,
                force_scalar_promotion=(
                    list(force_scalar_promotion) if force_scalar_promotion else []
                ),
                wrap_scalars=wrap_scalars,
                coerce_strings=coerce_strings,
                avro=True,
                map_encoding=map_encoding,
                wrap_root=wrap_root_field,
                no_root_map=no_root_map,
                max_builders=max_builders,
            )
            dtype = pl.Struct(schema)

        result = self._df.select(expr.str.json_decode(dtype=dtype))
        if unnest:
            result = result.unnest(expr.meta.output_name())
    else:
        result = self._df.select(expr).to_series()
    return result

def plug(expr: pl.Expr, changes_length: bool, **kwargs) -> pl.Expr:
    """Wrap Polars' `register_plugin_function` helper to always pass the same `lib`.

    Pass `changes_length` when using the `merge_schemas` (per-row) inference, as we only
    build a single schema in that case (so it'd be a waste to make more than one row).
    """
    func_name = inspect.stack()[1].function
    return register_plugin_function(
        plugin_path=lib,
        function_name=func_name,
        args=expr,
        is_elementwise=False,  # This is an aggregation across rows
        changes_length=changes_length,
        kwargs=kwargs,
    )

    map_encoding: Literal["entries", "mapping", "kv"] = "mapping",

    profile : bool, default False

    map_threshold : int, default 20

        Lower values reduce peak memory usage during schema inference.

    │ ---                                  │
    │ str                                  │

    │ {"id": "1", "labels": null}          │
    │ {"id": "2", "labels": {"en":"Hello"}}│
    └──────────────────────────────────────┘

        ignore_outer_array=ignore_outer_array,
        ndjson=ndjson,
        empty_as_null=empty_as_null,
        coerce_strings=coerce_strings,
        map_encoding=map_encoding,
        profile=profile,
        map_threshold=map_threshold,
        map_max_required_keys=map_max_required_keys,
        unify_maps=unify_maps,
        no_unify=no_unify,
        force_field_types=force_field_types,
        force_parent_field_types=force_parent_field_types,
        force_scalar_promotion=force_scalar_promotion,

        wrap_root=wrap_root,
        no_root_map=no_root_map,

        which is checked against the target (see `schema_check`), and written in the

def contains_map(dtype: pl.DataType) -> bool:

    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Map):

def project_dtype(
    expr: pl.Expr, have: pl.DataType, want: pl.DataType
) -> pl.Expr | None:
    """`expr`, of dtype `have`, as `str.json_decode` decodes the same values to `want`.

    `want`'s struct fields are taken by name (a field `have` lacks is null, one `want`
    lacks is dropped) and lists are projected element by element. ``None`` where the
    result could differ from `json_decode`'s: a leaf, map or array dtype other than
    `have`'s (where a cast and `json_decode`'s parse can disagree), or a nested `want`
    where `have` holds only nulls. Structs are built field by field, never cast, so
    no cast drops a struct field.
    """
    if have == want:
        return expr
    if isinstance(have, pl.Null):
        # Only nulls were seen there, and json_decode makes a null of any leaf dtype
        nested = (pl.Struct, pl.List, pl.Array, pl.Map)
        return None if isinstance(want, nested) else expr.cast(want)
    if isinstance(have, pl.Struct) and isinstance(want, pl.Struct):
        fields = {field.name: field.dtype for field in have.fields}
        parts = []
        for field in want.fields:
            if field.name in fields:
                part = project_dtype(
                    expr.struct.field(field.name), fields[field.name], field.dtype
                )
                if part is None:
                    return None
            else:
                # json_decode gives a field the JSON lacks as null (a null struct, not
                # a struct of nulls)
                part = pl.lit(None, dtype=field.dtype)
            parts.append(part.alias(field.name))
        # A null struct stays null, not a struct of null fields
        return pl.when(expr.is_not_null()).then(pl.struct(parts))
    if isinstance(have, pl.List) and isinstance(want, pl.List):
        inner = project_dtype(pl.element(), have.inner, want.inner)
        return None if inner is None else expr.list.eval(inner)
    return None

docs.title: typed_route_makes
docs.text:
typed_route_makes(dtype: DataType) -> bool

Whether dtype holds only dtypes the typed route can decode to.

Those are the ones avro_to_polars_schema gives an Avro schema: String, Int64, Float64, Boolean and Null leaves, in lists, structs and maps keyed by String. A dtype holding any other (Categorical, Int32, Datetime, Decimal, Array, ...) never projects, so it is decoded from JSON text without running the typed route first.

Source code in polars-genson-py/python/polars_genson/dtypes.py 
def typed_route_makes(dtype: pl.DataType) -> bool:
    """Whether `dtype` holds only dtypes the typed route can decode to.

    Those are the ones ``avro_to_polars_schema`` gives an Avro schema: String, Int64,
    Float64, Boolean and Null leaves, in lists, structs and maps keyed by String. A dtype
    holding any other (Categorical, Int32, Datetime, Decimal, Array, ...) never projects,
    so it is decoded from JSON text without running the typed route first.
    """
    # A field's dtype may be the class itself (pl.String) or an instance
    if any(
        dtype == leaf for leaf in (pl.String, pl.Int64, pl.Float64, pl.Boolean, pl.Null)
    ):
        return True
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.List):
        return typed_route_makes(dtype.inner)
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Struct):
        return all(typed_route_makes(field.dtype) for field in dtype.fields)
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Map):
        return dtype.key == pl.String and typed_route_makes(dtype.value)
    return False

docs.text:
dtype_spec(dtype: DataType | Schema) -> object

Describe a dtype (or a schema, as a struct of its columns) for a target schema.

The JSON-ready description the Rust side reads (genson_core::conform:: data_type_from_spec): a dtype name such as "String", or {"Struct": [[name, dtype], ...]}, {"List": dtype}, {"Array": [dtype, size]} or {"Map": [key, value]}.

Source code in polars-genson-py/python/polars_genson/dtypes.py 
def dtype_spec(dtype: pl.DataType | pl.Schema) -> object:
    """Describe a dtype (or a schema, as a struct of its columns) for a target schema.

    The JSON-ready description the Rust side reads (genson_core::conform::
    data_type_from_spec): a dtype name such as ``"String"``, or ``{"Struct": [[name,
    dtype], ...]}``, ``{"List": dtype}``, ``{"Array": [dtype, size]}`` or ``{"Map":
    [key, value]}``.
    """
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Schema):
        dtype = pl.Struct(dtype)
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Struct):
        return {"Struct": [[f.name, dtype_spec(f.dtype)] for f in dtype.fields]}
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.List):
        return {"List": dtype_spec(dtype.inner)}
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Array):
        return {"Array": [dtype_spec(dtype.inner), dtype.size]}
    if isinstance(dtype, pl.Map):
        return {"Map": [dtype_spec(dtype.key), dtype_spec(dtype.value)]}
    return str(dtype.base_type() if not isinstance(dtype, type) else dtype)

def parse_into_expr(
    expr: IntoExpr,
    *,
    str_as_lit: bool = False,
    list_as_lit: bool = True,
    dtype: PolarsDataType | None = None,
) -> pl.Expr:
    """Convert the user input into a polars.Expr.

    - If `expr` is already an `pl.Expr`, we return it as-is.
    - If `expr` is a string and `str_as_lit=False`, interpret as `pl.col(expr)`.
    - Otherwise, treat it as a literal (possibly typed by `dtype`).
    """
    if isinstance(expr, pl.Expr):
        return expr
    elif isinstance(expr, str) and not str_as_lit:
        return pl.col(expr)
    elif isinstance(expr, list) and not list_as_lit:
        return pl.lit(pl.Series(expr), dtype=dtype)
    else:
        return pl.lit(expr, dtype=dtype)
